title: Review of the thermals selection claim (SIMDH) on fresh seeds 31-36: S, M, D and heredity replicate; selection holds on 4 of 5 live paired seeds, seed 32 is null and seed 31 goes extinct before labelling
summary: labkit packs of the claimed world in both arms (eps -0.1 and the eps 0 twin, lab_mode 1, mut_dt 25) on fresh seeds 31 and 32, and the author's heredity2.py on paired seeds 32-36. Seed 31 burns out completely by t~100 in both arms (no caps ever form; 12/12 further seeds 33-44 survive to t=200, ext*.log). Seed 32: 39 persistent splits, generation 7 (selective arm); 10/15 dividing caps rise >= 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and division (2/15 by long axis), all with area jumps < 1.36. Daughters keep the parent's kind at 69/72, 90/90, 104/104, 108/108, 91/94 splits. The favoured kind b takes 0.81-0.91 of the caps on seeds 33-36 against 0.24-0.46 in the twin (births b:a 74:16, 100:4, 88:20, 83:11 vs 34:50, 20:42, 20:64, 22:56), but on seed 32 b does not rise (0.48 vs 0.54; births 33:39 vs 51:41) until the last ~150 t.

observations.S: rerun/sel/seed32/sheet.png t=0: a smoothed random hot field over the whole domain; caps re-nucleate from it after the field burns down (t=50-160). Note: lineage.png shows the whole population descends from ~2 caps that survive the burn-down, and seed 31 (rerun/sel/seed31/sheet.png) goes extinct by t~100 in both arms; 12/12 seeds 33-44 stay alive (ext1.log, ext2.log).
observations.I: rerun/sel/seed32/sheet.png t=313-1200: discrete crescent caps, 20-30 at a time, each persisting for tens of t between splits.
observations.M: rerun/sel/seed32/divmove.json: 10 of 15 dividing caps (born by a split, ending in a persistent split) rise >= 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and division, 13/15 travelling upward within 45 deg; e.g. track 144 born t=252, divides t=316, net 33.4 px = 6.7 sqrt(area) (4.1 long axes), max area jump 1.31. Caps are crescents moving broadside, so sqrt(area) is the protocol's unit; by long axis 2/15 pass. Neutral arm: 13/17 (6/17 long axis).
observations.D: rerun/sel/seed32/lineage.png: 39 persistent splits, generation 7; heredity2 counts 72-108 persistent splits after labelling on seeds 32-36.
observations.H: share_b_c55.png and heredity/h_*.json: daughters keep the parent's kind at 462/468 splits in the selective arm over seeds 32-36; kind changes of living caps fall at logged mutations 129/155 times. Favoured b reaches a mean share (t>=400) of 0.866/0.913/0.811/0.857 on seeds 33-36 vs 0.449/0.456/0.316/0.242 in the identical-draw twin, carried by births (b:a 74:16, 100:4, 88:20, 83:11 vs 34:50, 20:42, 20:64, 22:56). Seed 32 is null: 0.478 vs 0.537, births b:a 33:39 vs 51:41; b rises only after t~1000 (share 15/21 at t=1165).

seeds_run.result: fail: the random field burns out by t~100 in both arms, no caps form (rerun/*/seed31)
pass for S, I, M (10/15), D (39 splits, gen 7) and kind fidelity (69/72); null for selection (b share 0.48 vs 0.54)

controls_run.H: heredity/h_neu32-36.json: the author's eps 0 identical-draw twin run by me on seeds 32-36

verdicts.limitation: The selective arm also lowers the ancestor's yield (kind a burns at 0.9 Q, against Q for both kinds in the twin), so the twin does not share the ancestor's baseline fitness exactly; the selective arm has fewer caps early (seed 32: 5 vs 12 at t=245). Selection is not universal: 4 of 5 live paired seeds; on seed 32 the favoured kind stays near the twin's level for ~800 t. One of six fresh seeds goes extinct before any cap forms, and every population that does form descends from a handful of survivors of the initial burn-down. M is buoyant rise along gravity, measured in sqrt(area) for broadside crescents (by long axis 2/15 pass). No dt/2 or resolution re-run by me; B, E and X not checked.
